units.zh: 固雖君父，義有所不隆，及在臣子，或以行顯。
units.en: Thus even a ruler or father may lack exalted rightness, while a minister or son may be distinguished by conduct.
units.literal: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.

units.zh: 故能使上下邁德，罔有怠荒。
units.en: So it can make high and low advance in virtue, with none slack or negligent.
units.literal: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.

units.zh: 臣願聖世同符堯舜，行周同諡之禮，舍漢魏近制相避之議。」
units.en: I wish our sage age to match Yao and Shun, practicing the Zhou rite of shared titles and discarding the recent Han and Wei practice of avoidance."
units.literal: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”

units.zh: 又引周公父子同諡曰文。
units.en: They also cited the Duke of Zhou and his father, who shared the title Wen.
units.literal: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.

units.zh: 武帝詔曰：「非言君臣不可同，正以奕諡景不相當耳，宜諡曰簡。」
units.en: Emperor Wu decreed: "It is not that ruler and minister may never share a title; it is just that Jing does not suit Yi—he should be titled Jian."
units.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."

units.zh: 及太元四年，侍中王欣之表君臣之嫌同諡，尚書奏以欣之言為然。
units.en: In Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi objected that ruler and minister should not share a posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing endorsed his view.
units.literal: When it came to Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi memorialized that ruler and minister should avoid sharing the same posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing reported that Xinzhi's statement was correct.

units.zh: 詔可。
units.en: The edict approved it.
units.literal: The edict can be issued.

units.zh: 驃騎將軍溫嶠前妻李氏，在嶠微時便卒。
units.en: General of Agile Cavalry Wen Jiao's first wife, Lady Li, died when Jiao was still obscure.
units.literal: General Wen Qiao's ex-wife, Mrs. Li, died when Qiao was in decline.

units.zh: 又娶王氏、何氏，並在嶠前死。
units.en: He then married Lady Wang and Lady He, both of whom died before Jiao.
units.literal: He also married the Wang family and the He family, and died in Qiaoqian.

units.zh: 及嶠薨，朝廷以問陳舒：「三人並得為夫人不？」
units.en: When Jiao died, the court asked Chen Shu: "May all three be accorded the title of lady?"
units.literal: When Qiao died, the court asked Chen Shu: "Can the three of them be wives together?"

units.zh: 舒云：「《禮記》『其妻為夫人而卒，而後其夫不為大夫，而祔于其妻，則不易牲。
units.en: Shu said: "The Record of Rites says: 'If a wife died as a lady and afterward her husband ceased to be a grandee, when he is paired with his wife in sacrifice the victim is not changed.
units.literal: Shu Yun: "Book of Rites" "If his wife dies as his wife, and then her husband is not a high official, but his nephew is his wife, it is not easy to sacrifice him.

units.zh: 妻卒。
units.en: If the wife died
units.literal: His wife died.

units.zh: 而後夫為大夫，而祔于其妻，則以大夫牲』。
units.en: and afterward the husband became a grandee, when he is paired with his wife the grandee's victim is used.'
units.literal: If the later husband is a senior official and his wife is a nephew, then she will be sacrificed as a senior official."

units.zh: 然則夫榮于朝，妻貴于室，雖先夫沒，榮辱常隨於夫也。
units.en: So the husband is honored at court and the wife esteemed at home; though she died before her husband, honor and disgrace always follow the husband.
units.literal: However, the husband is honored in the court, and the wife is valued in the family. Even though the husband has passed away, the honor and disgrace will always follow the husband.

units.zh: 《禮記》曰『妻祔于祖姑，祖姑有三人，則祔其親者』。
units.en: The Record of Rites states: "A wife is paired in sacrifice with ancestresses (zu gu); when there are three ancestresses, she is paired with the one closest in degree."
units.literal: The Record of Rites states: "A wife is paired in sacrifice with ancestresses (zu gu); when there are three ancestresses, she is paired with the one closest in degree."

units.zh: 如禮，則三人皆為夫人也。
units.en: According to that ritual text, then all three may be titled ladies (furen).
units.literal: According to that ritual text, then all three may be titled ladies (furen).

units.zh: 自秦漢已來，廢一娶九女之制，近世無復繼室之禮，先妻卒則更娶。
units.en: Since Qin and Han, the system of one marriage bringing nine women has been abolished, and in recent ages there is no rite of successor consorts—when the first wife dies one remarries.
units.literal: Since the Qin and Han Dynasties, the system of marrying nine daughters to one woman has been abolished. In modern times, there is no such thing as the ritual of succession, and the first wife who dies will marry more.

units.zh: 苟生加禮，則亡不應貶。」
units.en: If rites are added to the living, the dead should not be demoted."
units.literal: If you add rituals in life, you should not be demoted in death."

units.zh: 庾蔚之云：「賤時之妻不得並為夫人，若有追贈之命則不論耳。」
units.en: Yu Weizhi said: "A wife from one's humble days may not share the title of lady, unless an order grants it posthumously."
units.literal: Yu Wei said: "Wives who were humble when they were young are not allowed to be wives. If there is a posthumous order, they will ignore it."

units.zh: 《嶠傳》，贈王、何二人夫人印綬，不及李氏，
units.en: The Biography of Jiao records that seals and ribbons of ladies were granted to Lady Wang and Lady He but not to Lady Li.
units.literal: "Qiao Zhuan", the seals and ribbons presented to Wang and He's wives are not as good as those of Li,

units.zh: 永和十一年，彭城國為李太妃求諡。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Yonghe, the state of Pengcheng requested a posthumous title for Consort Dowager Li.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Yonghe, Pengchengguo asked for the posthumous title of Concubine Li.

units.zh: 博士曹耽之議：「夫婦行不必同，不得以夫諡諡婦。
units.en: Erudite Cao Danzhi proposed: “Husband and wife need not have identical conduct, and one may not use the husband’s posthumous title to posthumously title the wife.
units.literal: Erudite Cao Danzhi proposed: “Husband and wife need not have identical conduct, and one may not use the husband’s posthumous title to posthumously title the wife.

units.zh: 《春秋》婦人有諡甚多，經無譏文，知禮得諡也。」
units.en: In the Spring and Autumn, women with posthumous titles are very numerous, and the classic has no text criticizing this; thus we know that according to ritual they may receive posthumous titles.”
units.literal: In the Spring and Autumn, women with posthumous titles are very numerous, and the classic has no text criticizing this; thus we know that according to ritual they may receive posthumous titles.”

units.zh: 胡訥云：「禮，婦人生以夫爵，死以夫諡。
units.en: Hu Na said: “According to ritual, a woman while living takes rank from her husband’s title, and when dead takes a posthumous title from her husband’s posthumous title.
units.literal: Hu Na said: “According to ritual, a woman while living takes rank from her husband’s title, and when dead takes a posthumous title from her husband’s posthumous title.

units.zh: 《春秋》夫人有諡，不復依禮耳。
units.en: That ladies in the Spring and Autumn have posthumous titles is simply that they did not again follow ritual.
units.literal: That ladies in the Spring and Autumn have posthumous titles is simply that they did not again follow ritual.

units.zh: 安平獻王李妃、琅邪武王諸葛妃，太傅東海王裴妃並無諡，今宜率舊典。」
units.en: Consort Li of King Xian of Anping, Consort Zhuge of King Wu of Langye, and Consort Pei of the Grand Tutor, the King of Donghai, all had no posthumous titles. Today it is fitting to follow the old canon.”
units.literal: Consort Li of King Xian of Anping, Consort Zhuge of King Wu of Langye, and Consort Pei of the Grand Tutor, the King of Donghai, all had no posthumous titles. Today it is fitting to follow the old canon.”

units.zh: 王彪之云：「婦人有諡，禮壞故耳。
units.en: Wang Biaozhi said: "That women have posthumous titles is only because ritual decayed.
units.literal: Wang Biao said: "A woman has a posthumous title, but her etiquette is bad.

units.zh: 聲子為諡，服虔諸儒以為非。
units.en: Shengzi received a posthumous title, and Fu Qian and other scholars thought it wrong.
units.literal: Shengzi was given a posthumous title, and the pious Confucians thought it was wrong.

units.zh: 杜預亦云『禮，婦人無諡』。
units.en: Du Yu also said, "With etiquette, a woman has no posthumous title."
units.literal: Du Yu also said, "With etiquette, a woman has no posthumous title."

units.zh: 《春秋》無譏之文，所謂不待貶絕自明者也。
units.en: The Spring and Autumn's lack of criticism is a case of fault so plain it needs no censure.
units.literal: There are no sarcastic articles in the Spring and Autumn Annals, as the so-called self-explanation does not require derogation.

units.zh: 近世惟后乃有諡耳。」
units.en: In recent ages only empresses receive posthumous titles."
units.literal: In modern times, there are posthumous titles only. "

units.zh: 太尉荀顗上諡法云：「若賜諡而道遠不及葬者，皆封策下屬，遣所承長吏奉策即塚祭賜諡。」，
units.en: Grand Commandant Xun Yi's rules on posthumous titles said: "If a title is granted but the road is too far to reach the burial, the patent is sealed and sent down, and the responsible senior official carries it to the tomb to sacrifice and bestow the title."
units.literal: Taiwei Xunyi's posthumous law says: "If a posthumous title is given but the road is far from being able to bury the person, all the officials will be appointed as subordinates, and the senior officials will be sent to carry out the posthumous ceremony at the tomb to offer the posthumous title.",

units.zh: 太元十三年，召孔安國為侍中。
units.en: In Taiyuan 13, Kong Anguo was summoned as Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In Taiyuan 13, Kong Anguo was summoned to serve as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 安國表以黃門郎王愉名犯私諱，不得連署，求解。
units.en: Kong Anguo memorialized that Wang Yu's name violated his private taboo, making him unable to co-sign, and asked to be relieved.
units.literal: Anguo memorialized that Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Wang Yu's name violated his private taboo, so he could not co-sign, and he requested to be relieved.

units.zh: 有司議云：「名終諱之，有心所同，聞名心瞿，亦明前誥。
units.en: The officials said: "A name is tabooed at death, a feeling all share; hearing the name startles the heart, as earlier precepts also make clear.
units.literal: Some officials said: "The name is taboo, and it has the same mind. It is famous for its heart Qu, and it is also clear from the previous imperial edict.

units.zh: 而《禮》復云『君所無私諱，大夫之所有公諱』，無私諱。
units.en: Yet the Rites also say, 'In the ruler's presence there are no private taboos; in a grandee's presence there are public taboos'—that is, no private taboos.
units.literal: And the "Li" further says, "What the ruler has no selfish taboos for, all the officials have public taboos for." It is selfless taboos.

units.zh: 又云『詩書不諱，臨文不諱』。
units.en: It also says, 'There is no taboo in the Odes and the Documents, nor when handling written texts.'
units.literal: It is also said that "the poems and books do not conceal anything, and the texts do not conceal anything".

units.zh: 豈非公義奪私情，王制屈家禮哉！
units.en: Is this not public duty overriding private feeling, royal law bending family rites!
units.literal: Isn't it true that justice takes over personal love, and the king controls family etiquette?

units.zh: 尚書安眾男臣先表中兵曹郎王祐名犯父諱，求解職，明詔爰發，聽許換曹，蓋是恩出制外耳。
units.en: Your servant, Minister and Baron of Anzhong, earlier memorialized that the name of Wang You, Gentleman of the Central Troops Section, violated his father's taboo and that he asked to be relieved of office; a clear edict was issued permitting a change of section—an act of grace beyond the rules.
units.literal: Shangshu An and all the male ministers first asked for the dismissal of Cao Lang and Wang You, who had violated his father's name. He issued an imperial edict and promised to change Cao. It was a kindness to control the outer ear.

units.zh: 而頃者互相瞻式，源流既啟，莫知其極。
units.en: But lately people imitate one another; once the stream has begun, no one knows where it will end.
units.literal: But for a moment, they looked at each other, and the source and flow had begun, but they didn't know the end.

units.zh: 夫皇朝禮大，百僚備職，編官列署，動相經涉。
units.en: The imperial court's rites are great: the hundred officials fill their posts, offices are ranged in bureaus, and their business constantly crosses one another's.
units.literal: The husband's imperial court was full of ceremony, hundreds of officials were prepared for their posts, officials were listed in the department, and everything was done.

units.zh: 若以私諱，人遂其心，則移官易職，遷流莫已，既違典法，有虧政體。
units.en: If private taboos let people follow their wishes, offices will shift endlessly—against the statutes and harmful to government.
units.literal: If people use personal taboos to follow their own will, they will be moved to different positions or moved to other places, which is against the law and is detrimental to the political system.

units.zh: 請一斷之。」
units.en: We ask for a single ruling."
units.literal: Please cut it off.”

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: This was followed.
units.literal: Follow it.
